papers.title: Phonon-mediated spin-spin interactions
papers.summary: A theory of phonon-mediated interactions derives symmetric and antisymmetric couplings between localized magnetic moments. Broken inversion symmetry is required for the antisymmetric contribution, with predicted temperature and distance dependences.
papers.whyRelevant: Provides a complementary mechanism to consider when connecting chirality, lattice motion and effective spin interactions.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect chiral or inversion-asymmetric environments with spin–phonon physics.

papers.title: Quantum Mpemba effect: anomalous relaxation of multi-spin system under local noise
papers.authors: Xiao-Xu Ning, Zhen-Dong Wei, Wei-Bin Yan, Zhong-Xiao Man, Yun-Jie Xia, Ying-Jie Zhang, Qing-Yu Cai
papers.summary: An open central-spin model exhibits relaxation-order reversals under suitable initial states and local noise. The analysis explores how spin number, global rotations and nonuniform decoherence influence the quantum Mpemba effect.
papers.whyRelevant: Useful theoretical context for interpreting relaxation curves when the environment and preparation both matter.

relatedPapers.reason: Both treat spin relaxation using explicit dynamical models.

papers.title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
papers.authors: Aleksandr Shlykov, Meissa L. Diouf, Richard Karl, Mikolaj Roguski, Umesh C. Joshi, Stefan Willitsch
papers.summary: Quantum-logic spectroscopy resolves electric-quadrupole vibrational transitions in a single trapped nitrogen molecular ion. The experiment identifies hyperfine-resolved components and demonstrates coherent population transfer between molecular energy levels.
papers.whyRelevant: An adjacent molecular platform illustrating how complex internal structure can be resolved and coherently addressed.

relatedPapers.reason: Both demonstrate coherent addressing of molecular quantum states, with different physical encodings.

papers.title: Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array
papers.authors: Yi-Hsien Wu, Leon C. Camenzind, Patrick Bütler, Ik Kyeong Jin, Akito Noiri, Kenta Takeda, Takashi Nakajima, Takashi Kobayashi, Giordano Scappucci, Hsi-Sheng Goan, Seigo Tarucha
papers.summary: Experiments identify drive-induced AC-Stark shifts as a limiting factor in simultaneous silicon-spin operations. Pairwise phase calibrations and tailored pulses preserve high fidelity across parallel control in a five-qubit array.
papers.whyRelevant: A transferable calibration idea for studying cross-talk, although the experimental platform is semiconductor rather than molecular spins.

relatedPapers.reason: Both require precise control and calibration of electron-spin transitions.

papers.title: Instability-enhanced quantum sensing with tunable multibody interactions
papers.authors: Bidhi Vijaywargia, Jorge Chávez-Carlos, Francisco Pérez-Bernal, Lea F. Santos
papers.summary: A theoretical extension of a collective-spin sensing Hamiltonian adds multibody interactions that accelerate signal amplification. The analysis shows that local phase-space curvature matters alongside the instability rate for finite-time metrological gain.
papers.whyRelevant: A comparison point for assessing interaction-enhanced sensing beyond simple coherence-time arguments.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use spin dynamics to encode environmental information, in different regimes.

papers.title: High-density optical quantum sensors with pulsed probe read-out for correlated spin-noise reduction
papers.summary: Pulsed optical readout in a potassium-vapor sensor reveals temporal correlations in the measured noise. Phase cycling and delayed subtraction suppress or diagnose reproducible contributions; the authors explicitly do not claim independently established spin squeezing.
papers.whyRelevant: A useful example of distinguishing noise correlations from demonstrated quantum enhancement.

relatedPapers.reason: Both focus on artifact-aware processing of quantum-sensor measurements.

papers.title: Observable scaling hierarchies in multiphoton dissipative quantum sensing
papers.summary: A theoretical study separates scaling in multiphoton fluctuations from scaling in measured observables under squeezed driving. It shows that the accessible sensitivity depends on the correlation structure and the chosen measurement.
papers.whyRelevant: Helps avoid equating a promising quantum fluctuation resource with an automatically observable sensing advantage.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect measurement choices with the information retained in a sensor signal.

papers.title: Framework Deuteration Regulates Excited-State Dynamics and H2O2 Release in Covalent Organic Framework Photocatalysis
papers.authors: Zhengrong Xu, Shihang Yu, Xinxin Chen, Tian Zhang, Dong Lv, Tianqi Liu, Aiguo Kong, Xiaolei Fan, Rui Liu
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Matched hydrogenated and deuterated COFs isolate isotope effects without changing framework connectivity. Spectroscopy and calculations associate deuteration with altered exciton–phonon coupling, excited-state lifetimes and product-release energetics in photocatalysis.
papers.whyRelevant: Isotope substitution offers a controlled way to investigate vibrational effects; the reported observable is photocatalysis rather than spin coherence.

relatedPapers.reason: Both motivate studying how lattice vibrations influence molecular-state dynamics.

papers.title: Isoreticular Contraction of kgd‐Topology Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Pharmaceutical Separation
papers.authors: Baodong Tian, Hukang Guo, Weilin Feng, Jiaqi Li, Wenshuo Cui, Chuanjie Fang, Li Xu, Liping Zhu
papers.summary: An isoreticular series of COF membranes narrows pore apertures by changing monomer size during interfacial polymerization. The authors combine membranes with distinct rejection thresholds into a cascade separation system.
papers.whyRelevant: Offers a controlled synthesis example for tuning framework geometry while preserving a common topology.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect controlled framework formation to structurally defined materials.

papers.title: Control-Noise Trade-offs in Industrially Integrated ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ Spin-1/2 Qubits
papers.authors: Leon C. Camenzind, Ik Kyeong Jin, Yi-Hsien Wu, Akito Noiri, Kenta Takeda, Takashi Nakajima, Takashi Kobayashi, Giordano Scappucci, Seigo Tarucha
papers.summary: Foundry-integrated silicon spin qubits exhibit high-fidelity gates while revealing a placement-dependent trade-off between electrical drive strength and charge-noise sensitivity. Micromagnet separation changes both longitudinal noise conversion and transverse control efficiency.
papers.whyRelevant: A solid-state benchmark for balancing coherent control against environmental noise, not a molecular-qubit demonstration.

relatedPapers.reason: A solid-state benchmark for balancing coherent control against environmental noise, not a molecular-qubit demonstration.

papers.title: DMF-Driven Modulation of Coordination Geometry and SMM Performance in Dinuclear Dysprosium(III) Complexes
papers.authors: Xiaofang Li, Hongling Lv, Liang Zheng, Zaiheng Yao, Yan Fan, Laxiang Yang, Mingfei Xu, Zilu Chen
papers.summary: Adding coordinated DMF changes the geometry of dinuclear dysprosium complexes and their measured magnetic relaxation barriers. Electronic-structure calculations relate the difference to anisotropy and local coordination.
papers.whyRelevant: A comparative molecular-magnet example of environment-dependent relaxation; qubit coherence would require separate measurements.

relatedPapers.reason: A comparative molecular-magnet example of environment-dependent relaxation; qubit coherence would require separate measurements.

papers.title: Helper-assisted quantum sensing with low dressed-state leakage
papers.summary: A two-qubit model encodes a signal in an auxiliary qubit while limiting sensor excitation and dressed-state leakage. Simulations examine reset costs, offsets and noise-model errors; practical advantages over direct readout depend on device-specific disturbance.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant to minimally disturbing spin readout and sensor–ancilla architectures, with explicit limits on the claimed advantage.

relatedPapers.reason: Relevant to minimally disturbing spin readout and sensor–ancilla architectures, with explicit limits on the claimed advantage.

papers.title: Biorthogonal universal quantum control
papers.summary: A biorthogonal control framework constructs transitionless pathways for non-Hermitian systems. Three-level examples illustrate population transfer and a holonomic gate, including conditions under which nonunitary intermediate dynamics yield a unitary final transformation.
papers.whyRelevant: An adjacent theoretical route for pulse design in open systems; implementation in molecular spins remains to be assessed.

relatedPapers.reason: An adjacent theoretical route for pulse design in open systems; implementation in molecular spins remains to be assessed.

papers.title: Anion-Directed Structural Modulation and Tunable Luminescence in Copper(I)–Organic Hybrids
papers.authors: Gopendra Muduli, Bikash Lahkar, Pragadeeswara Venkatamani Gunasekaran, Ranjan Kumar Sahu, Sriram Chintu Banoth, Abhilash Sahu, Kohsuke Matsumoto, Osamu Tsutsumi, François Réveret, Federico Cisnetti, Saket Asthana, Ganesan Prabusankar
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.archiveJournal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: Sonochemical assembly with different anions changes copper–organic hybrids from chain-like to layered structures. Crystallography and optical studies connect coordination and connectivity with the character and color of solid-state emission.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant to framework-structure control using a fixed ligand and altered coordination partners.

relatedPapers.reason: Relevant to framework-structure control using a fixed ligand and altered coordination partners.
